audit_findings.title: Forecast may omit the disclosed step-change in required capital spending
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.0 billion planned 2026 capital expenditures; $493.3 million spent in 1H 2026, equal to 76.0% of $649.0 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Forecast OE and growth reinvestment would be overstated if the capacity spending and associated working capital are not deducted or reconciled to incremental earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate our 2026 capital expenditures to be approximately $1 billion (about 6% of currently anticipated revenue), a significant increase over our historical capital expenditure range of 1.5% to 2.0% of annual revenue, to support expected growth in customer demand, particularly from our hyperscaler customers.
audit_findings.explanation: The spending step-change is demonstrated, but its omission from forecast cash flow is an unresolved possibility. The disclosed annual spending is 154% of anchor OE and about 10.4% of base equity value, so an unreconciled portion could materially change value. The generic 36% RONTA assumption does not itself demonstrate that the actual capacity build, customer funding and working-capital requirements were captured.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile annual 2026-2027 capital expenditures, customer reimbursements, disposal proceeds and working-capital investment to forecast OE and credited growth, then rerun every scenario using the reconciled cash flows.

audit_findings.title: The terminal tax burden may capitalize expiring tax holidays
audit_findings.magnitude: $51 million FY2025 tax-incentive benefit, equal to 7.9% of $649.0 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: An abnormally low tax burden raises anchor OE and, if perpetuated, forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We have been granted certain income tax incentives in Thailand, including tax holidays, that will expire in whole or in part at various dates during 2027 through 2029, unless extended or otherwise renegotiated.
audit_findings.explanation: Expiration during 2027-2029 and the $51 million 2025 benefit are demonstrated; indefinite capitalization by the model remains an unresolved possibility because no post-expiry tax normalization is shown. A recurring amount equal to 7.9% of anchor OE is material, particularly because terminal value represents 47.7%-51.5% of operating value.
audit_findings.action: Separate recurring cash taxes from the $68.1 million deferred-tax-asset recognition and other discrete items, forecast jurisdictional cash taxes through the 2027-2029 expirations, document any renewal assumption and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Not all cash in the equity bridge is necessarily excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $481.4 million customer deposits versus $535.7 million cash added at 2026-06-30; exact non-excess cash amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding operating, restricted or deposit-backed cash in the equity bridge can double-count funds required to support inventory and working-capital obligations already reflected in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We receive cash deposits from certain of our customers primarily to help reduce risks related to excess and/or obsolete inventory.
audit_findings.explanation: The full cash addition and $481.4 million deposit liability are demonstrated, but the amount of cash that is unavailable to owners is not. The deposits equal 89.9% of cash and 5.0% of base equity value, before considering minimum operating cash or repatriation taxes, making the unresolved bridge adjustment reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Produce a June 30 cash-surplus schedule reconciling customer deposits, inventory commitments, minimum operating cash, geographic restrictions and repatriation taxes; replace the bridge addition with demonstrably distributable cash and rerun per-share values.

audit_findings.title: The TRS creates an omitted market-dependent claim or asset
audit_findings.magnitude: $94.3 million filed asset at 2026-06-30, equal to 1.0% of $9,654 million base equity value and $0.80 per share; approximately $36.7 million gross mark at the $312.35 valuation price before financing costs
audit_findings.mechanism: The net TRS fair value belongs in the equity bridge, while fair-value movements should remain excluded from OE and periodic financing costs retained in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Similarly, if the value of the TRS Agreement decreases over the term of the TRS Agreement, we are obligated to pay the counterparty the amount of such decrease upon Settlement.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 30 TRS asset and its omission from the displayed bridge are demonstrated. Its filed amount is only about 1.0% of base equity value, and the valuation-date gross mark computed from 1.25 million shares, the $288.87 strike and $312.35 share price is about 0.4% of base equity value. This scale cannot materially alter the valuation conclusion, although the bridge should still be corrected.
audit_findings.action: Confirm post-quarter settlements, re-strikes, accrued financing and the September 5 net fair value; add the resulting net asset or liability to the bridge and verify that only fair-value movements—not periodic financing costs—were purged from OE.

audit_findings.title: Existing pension underfunding is a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $84.8 million FY2025 net deficit, equal to 0.9% of $9,654 million base equity value and $0.72 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A pre-existing unfunded benefit obligation reduces the equity bridge unless forecast OE includes catch-up contributions beyond recurring benefit cost.
audit_findings.evidence: Although we have defined benefit plans that are currently in a net unfunded position, we do not expect our pension obligations will have a material adverse impact on our future results of operations, cash flows or liquidity.
audit_findings.explanation: The $84.8 million net deficit is demonstrated. Even deducting the entire gross deficit without tax relief would reduce base value by only $0.72 per share, versus the reported $82.28 base value, so it is not material to the conclusion. The June 2026 net funded status and payment timing remain to be updated.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30 funded-status schedule and forecast contributions exceeding recurring service cost; deduct the after-tax uncovered deficit or document where catch-up payments are already included in forecast OE.

audit_findings.title: Flat-growth bear case still perpetuates a concentrated peak earnings level
audit_findings.mechanism: Using $649.0 million as the perpetual starting OE level makes the bear case depend on maintaining peak customer volumes, mix and margins; customer or program normalization would reduce anchor OE rather than merely growth.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, three customers (all in our CCS segment) individually represented 10% or more of total revenue (32%, 14% and 12%).
audit_findings.explanation: The concentration is demonstrated: the three largest customers represented 58% of 2025 revenue and 63% of Q2 2026 revenue, while 2025 OE rose 58.2% from 2024. No customer-level profit data establishes the size of a sustainable-OE adjustment, so the error is not demonstrated. Nevertheless, the concentration and rapid ramp make an earnings-level decline reasonably capable of materially changing every scenario, and 0% growth does not test that risk.
audit_findings.action: Obtain customer and program contribution margins, ramp costs, contract duration and normalized utilization data; derive a sustainable OE anchor and rerun explicit customer-loss, program-transition and margin-normalization downside cases rather than only a 0% growth case.
